perf_annotate_hot_lines.note: The hottest single instruction (11.32%) is a stack spill of lua_max_call_frames — the result of activeErrorHandlerDepth() call that runs every activation but is only consumed in the near-overflow branch. This is pure register pressure: the result occupies a callee-saved register across the entire function, causing spills in the field-write section.

classification.description: Classification of every operation in pushBytecodeExecFrame for the common non-vararg Lua-to-Lua case (args_on_stack=true, is_vahid=false, no overflow).

operations.note: Diagnostic counter, gated by stats.enabled (default-off). The branch is per-activation; the increment is conditional. Could be classified as hooks-debug-only since the value is only consumed by diagnostics, but the branch itself is per-activation overhead.

Checks proto.constants_resolved flag, returns early if already done. One-time cost per Proto: interns string constants + pre-resolves all constants into resolved_values array. After first execution, this is a single branch (predicted-not-taken).

Calls activeErrorHandlerDepth() (which calls activeBytecodeThread() + reads 2 fields) every activation. The result (lua_max_call_frames = 10000 or 1000000) is ONLY consumed in the near-overflow branch (exec_frames.len() >= lua_max_call_frames). In the common case (frame count << 10000), the specific value is irrelevant. The call causes register pressure: its result is spilled to stack (11.32% of function overhead per perf annotate). Could be deferred to inside the overflow branch.
Compile-time constants, zero runtime cost. Listed for completeness.
Needed for needed_top computation, regs slice, and frame field write.
Needed for nextra, nil-fill, nvarstack, reg_top field writes.
For non-vararg: proto.is_vararg is false, short-circuits to 0. The branch is predicted-not-taken but still per-activation. Result (0) is written to nextraargs field.
For non-vararg: false via short-circuit on proto.is_vararg. Used to gate buildhiddenargs and func_slot computation.
Pure alias, zero runtime cost.

Pointer comparison: args.ptr == bc_stack.ptr + (func_slot_in + 1) * @sizeOf(Value). For OP_CALL fast path: true (args already on stack). The check itself is the per-activation cost — it decides whether to copy args.

Only executed when args come from heap/host (runBytecodeInternal, builtin pcall, metamethods, debug hooks, coroutine resume). NOT executed on OP_CALL fast path. Includes ensureBcStackCap + func write + args copy loop.
Pure alias, zero runtime cost.
For non-vararg: func_slot = func_slot_in (predicted branch). Result needed for base computation and all field writes.
Needed for regs slice, needed_top, and all field writes. Core frame geometry.
PUC ltm.c buildhiddenargs: shifts func+params UP past extra args. NOT executed for non-vararg. Includes ensureBcStackCap + copy + nil-fill.
Needed for overflow check and ensureBcStackCap.

The bc_stack.len > 1M comparison runs every activation (cheap, almost always false). The activeErrorHandlerDepth() call is only reached when bc_stack.len > 1M (short-circuit AND). The body (handler overflow check) is error-handler-only.

operations.operation: stack overflow checks (exec_frames.len() >= lua_max_call_frames or needed_top > lua_stack_overflow_limit)
operations.note: The comparisons run every activation but are almost always false (frame count << 10000, stack pre-allocated). The body (realloc to ERRORSTACKSIZE + fail) only executes on actual overflow.
Capacity check is per-activation (compares needed_top vs bc_stack.len). The grow path is near-stack-overflow-only. In the common case, this is a single comparison + branch.
Must set bc_stack_top to needed_top for the new frame. errdefer restores on error (zero cost on success path).
Needed for nil-fill and returned to caller via ctx. Pure slice arithmetic (pointer + length).
For common case (nargs >= nparams): ncopy = nparams, loop for (ncopy..nparams) does not execute. Just the @min + branch. The nil-fill only runs when nargs < nparams (host-recursion with fewer args).
Saves bc_tbc_regs.items.len for errdefer rollback on frame pop. Zero cost on success path (just a field read + errdefer setup).

3rd call to activeBytecodeThread() in the function. Cannot be CSE-d with earlier calls because ensureBcStackCap (line 11221) is between them and may modify self. However, activeBytecodeThread() only reads self.current_thread/self.main_thread which ensureBcStackCap does not modify — so the compiler MAY CSE this in ReleaseFast with inlining.
Incrementing overflow counter for frame identity in syncFrame. Wrap protection (if == 0, set to 1) is rarely taken but the check is per-activation.

Grows frame stack by one. Checks inline_count < INLINE_FRAME_CAP: returns inline slot (cheap) or heap.addOne (alloc). In common case (shallow call depth), uses inline slot — just a counter increment + pointer arithmetic.
Error handling infrastructure. Zero cost on success path.

Must activate .lua variant before writing .u.lua fields. In ReleaseFast: zero cost (undefined = no-op). In Debug: safety check. Required for correctness when reusing a slot that previously held a .c variant.
Core frame field: needed for dispatch (opcode fetch, constant access).
Initial program counter for the new frame.
Number of stack-visible variables. Needed for VARARG, return handling, stack top tracking.
Frame identity for syncFrame validation. syncFrame checks activation_id == frame_identity to detect frame realloc invalidation.
Stack base for the frame. Needed for regs/boxed slice derivation, stack top restoration on pop.
Callee position on bc_stack (PUC ci->func). Needed for callee access, upvalue derivation, tail call.
Original func slot before VAHID shift. Needed for VAHID unwind and tail call base restoration. For non-vararg: equals func_slot (redundant write, but needed for the vararg case).
Frame capacity (maxstacksize + EXTRA_MARGIN). Needed for regs/boxed slice derivation, stack top computation.
For non-vararg: always 0. Only read by VARARG/return paths for vararg functions. The write itself is per-activation but the value is only consumed for vararg functions.
Encodes nresults + clears all flag bits (CIST_TAIL, CIST_HOOKED, etc.). Needed for return handling.
Needed for coroutine yield/resume. Must be initialized to avoid stale data from frame reuse.
Register top (number of live registers). Needed for stack top tracking, GC scanning.
Only read by line hooks (debug.sethook with "l" mask). Written every activation to prevent stale data from frame reuse. Could be lazily initialized when hooks are first activated.
Only read by line hook dispatch. Written every activation for stale-data prevention. Could be lazily initialized.
TBC (to-be-closed) mark for frame pop cleanup. Needed for correct TBC variable scoping.
Must clear stale state from frame reuse. pending_call_index is read by return/continue paths to check if a pending call exists.
Only read by call hook dispatch. Written every activation for stale-data prevention. Could be lazily initialized.
Must clear stale simple-result state from frame reuse. simple_result is read by return paths to check if a simple-result completion is pending.
Must clear stale open-upvalues flag from frame reuse. Read by upvalue scanning paths.
Only read by count hook dispatch after coroutine resume. Written every activation for stale-data prevention. Could be lazily initialized.

optimization_opportunities.impact: 11.32% of pushBytecodeExecFrame overhead (hottest single instruction — stack spill of result)
optimization_opportunities.fix: Defer the activeErrorHandlerDepth() call to inside the near-overflow branch. Compute lua_max_call_frames lazily only when exec_frames.len() >= 10000 (the lower limit). This eliminates the per-activation call + stack spill.
optimization_opportunities.risk: Low — the error handler depth cannot change during pushBytecodeExecFrame. The only semantic change is that the overflow check uses 10000 (the error-handler limit) as the threshold for calling activeErrorHandlerDepth(), which is correct since 10000 is the lower of the two limits.

optimization_opportunities.operation: Debug field writes (last_line_pc, skip_line_hook_pc, skip_call_hook_pc, resume_skip_count_pc)
optimization_opportunities.impact: ~4 field writes per activation, each costing a mov instruction. Estimated ~4-6% of function overhead based on perf annotate (INVALID_PC writes are among the hottest instructions).
optimization_opportunities.fix: Lazy initialization: write these fields only when hooks are first activated for a frame. Requires a "hooks ever active" flag per frame or a generation check. Alternatively, batch-clear all debug fields in a single memset when entering hook mode.
optimization_opportunities.risk: Medium — must ensure no code path reads these fields before they are initialized. The frame reuse stale-data concern must be addressed by the lazy-init mechanism.

optimization_opportunities.impact: 1 field write per activation. Small but nonzero.
optimization_opportunities.fix: Could skip the write for non-vararg functions (the field is already 0 from a previous non-vararg frame, or could be set to 0 by addOne). But frame reuse means the slot may contain stale data from a previous vararg frame.
optimization_opportunities.risk: Low — but requires proving that nextraargs is only read for vararg functions, and that no non-vararg frame ever reads it.
